text: Nathalie Ménigon, born on 28 February 1957 in Enghien-les-Bains, Val-d'Oise, was convicted for acts of terrorism committed during her time as a member of the French revolutionary group Action Directe. She was sentenced to life in prison in 1989 for the 1986 assassination of Georges Besse, then-president of Renault, and the 1985 assassination of René Audran, a senior official at the French Ministry of Defence. She was arrested on 18 February 1987, along with Jean-Marc Rouillan, Joëlle Aubron, and Georges Cipriani, at a farm in Vitry-aux-Loges. She married Jean-Marc Rouillan on 29 June 1999 at Fleury-Mérogis Prison. Imprisoned at Bapaume Prison in Pas-de-Calais until August 2007, she was three times denied a suspended sentence due to medical conditions, including hemiplegia, depression, balance problems, and spasms. In May 2007, she was transferred to a house arrest program that allowed her to work during the day but required her to spend nights in prison, a condition necessary for her eventual conditional release. Her conditional release became effective on 2 August 2008. While in prison, she suffered from hemiplegia resulting from two strokes and engaged in self-harm in 2003 as a protest against jail conditions. In July 2008, she expressed interest in the New Anticapitalist Party, founded by Olivier Besancenot and the Revolutionary Communist League.
